subject: Novapulse private deployment — integration checklist & operational schedule
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novapulse.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@novapulse.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novapulse private deployment: integration checklist & ops questions

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move toward an on-prem/private deployment for our PHI workloads. Before we schedule a technical kickoff, procurement and engineering asked for a concise checklist and a couple of clarifications so they can validate timelines with our security and network teams. Can you confirm the following?

1) Do you provide an operator-run offline installation path (air-gapped) and an operator checklist for patching/updates?
2) Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for key wrapping and support rotation policies?
3) What network egress rules are required for the control plane vs. the runtime nodes? We need a minimal whitelist to get through our reviewers.
4) Expected window for a standard Private (VPC) install — from kickoff to production readiness — assuming Novapulse provides a 3-node GPU cluster and a named SRE.

Could you attach any example runbooks, network diagram templates, and an ops checklist? Procurement (copied) also needs to know if we can get a bill-of-materials for capital planning.

Appreciate it — can we get these by EOD Monday so we can brief leadership?

—Alex
Alex Turner
Director of Engineering, Novapulse Health
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novapulse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@novapulse.com
Date: 2026-07-19T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novapulse private deployment: integration checklist & ops questions

Hi Alex — thanks, and great to hear Novapulse is moving forward. Attaching a compact package to cover the items you listed: a one-page deployment checklist (novapulse-deploy-checklist.pdf), a network diagram template (network-diagram-template.svg), and an ops play summary. High-level answers below; full details in the attachments.

1) Air-gapped/offline install: Yes. We support an operator-driven airgap install flow. The checklist includes steps for seed artifact ingestion, signature verification, and an offline licensing mechanism. Patching is operator-initiated; we provide signed delta bundles and a validation step.

2) KMS/HSM integration: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for envelope encryption and key wrapping. We also support HSM-backed key stores via PKCS#11 and integrate with AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, and on-prem HSM appliances. We document rotation and re-wrapping procedures in Section 3 of the checklist.

3) Network egress: Minimal runtime egress is required for license rechecks (configurable) and optional telemetry. The control plane (if you use Redwood-managed control) requires outbound to control.redwoodinference.com over 443; runtime nodes can be configured for zero outbound (fully air-gapped) with pre-seeded artifacts. The network template highlights required ports and CIDR suggestions.

4) Timeline to production: Typical timeline is 4–6 weeks for a standard Private deployment (kickoff, environment prep, install, smoke, production handoff) if networking and hardware are ready. For fully air-gapped installs add 1–2 weeks for artifact transfer and validation. We included a suggested kickoff agenda and a list of roles/responsibilities.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether you want Redwood to operate the control plane (hosted) or for us to provide a private control plane bundle to run in your VPC.
- Proposed tech kickoff times: Tue 2026-07-21 11:00–12:00 PT or Wed 2026-07-22 09:00–10:00 PT.

If either time works I’ll send a calendar invite and our pre-kickoff checklist for your SREs.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Novapulse private deployment: integration checklist & ops questions

Alex — quick technical note to supplement Chloe’s package:

- Airgap installation detail: we provide signed artifact bundles and a checksum manifest. The operator transfers bundles via secure media and runs our verifier which checks signatures against a root PGP key we deliver separately. That keeps the runtime deterministic and auditable.
- Licensing & updates: offline license validation uses a time-bounded license file; if you prefer, we can implement a local license server that your SREs host behind the firewall to avoid outbound checks.
- Hardware/driver matrix: if you plan to use mixed GPU types, let us know the models so we can provide a tuned kernel/quantization profile.

Attaching a short ops note (airgap-install-ops-notes.txt) that walks through the artifact transfer and operator steps. Happy to cover these in the kickoff.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
